paragraphs.title: The Strange Fire and the Death of Aaron’s Sons

easy.question: Who offered the strange fire before the Lord?
answers: Nadab and Abihu
Moses and Aaron
The Israelites
easy.explanation: Nadab and Abihu, Aaron’s sons, offered the strange fire before the Lord.

easy.question: What happened to Nadab and Abihu after they offered the strange fire?
answers: They left the tabernacle
Fire went out from the Lord, consumed them, and they died
They received a blessing
easy.explanation: The passage says that fire went out from the Lord, consumed them, and they died.

easy.question: How did Aaron respond after Moses spoke?
answers: He spoke to the people
He left the tabernacle
He remained silent
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying, “And Aaron held his peace,” meaning that Aaron remained silent.

medium.question: Why were Nadab and Abihu punished, according to the verse?
answers: Because they offered fire that the Lord had not commanded
Because they did not bring incense
Because they were late for their tabernacle service
medium.explanation: The verse emphasizes that they offered “strange fire,” which the Lord had not commanded.

medium.question: In the phrase “each took his censer,” what is a censer?
answers: A special garment
A container for holding fire or incense
A place where someone lives
medium.explanation: Each man took a censer, put fire in it, and placed incense on it; it was a vessel used for incense service.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Aaron was silent, then they offered incense, and Moses spoke
Moses spoke, then fire went out, and they took censers
Nadab and Abihu offered fire, fire went out from the Lord, and Moses spoke to Aaron
medium.explanation: First Aaron’s sons offered strange fire, then fire went out from the Lord, and finally Moses spoke to Aaron.

challenge.question: What does the statement “I will be sanctified in them that come near me” suggest about Nadab and Abihu?
answers: They served near the Lord and therefore had to be especially careful
They were far from the tabernacle
They were not involved in holy service
challenge.explanation: Moses explains that the Lord is sanctified among those who come near Him; therefore, those who serve before Him must obey His commands carefully.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the fire from the Lord consumed Nadab and Abihu?
answers: The fire was only part of a festive ceremony
The event was understood as an immediate divine response to their act
The people were the ones who punished them
challenge.explanation: The close connection between their offering of strange fire and the fire from the Lord shows an immediate response to an act they had not been commanded to perform.

challenge.question: Why did Moses speak to Aaron specifically after the death of his sons?
answers: To ask him to prepare new incense
To tell him to leave his position
To explain the meaning of the event and emphasize the Lord’s glory
challenge.explanation: Moses interprets their deaths as part of the Lord’s being sanctified before the people and emphasizes that holy service must honor Him.

questions.question: What does the statement “I will be sanctified in them that come near me” suggest about Nadab and Abihu?
answers: They served near the Lord and therefore had to be especially careful
They were far from the tabernacle
They were not involved in holy service
questions.explanation: Moses explains that the Lord is sanctified among those who come near Him; therefore, those who serve before Him must obey His commands carefully.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the fire from the Lord consumed Nadab and Abihu?
answers: The fire was only part of a festive ceremony
The event was understood as an immediate divine response to their act
The people were the ones who punished them
questions.explanation: The close connection between their offering of strange fire and the fire from the Lord shows an immediate response to an act they had not been commanded to perform.

questions.question: Why did Moses speak to Aaron specifically after the death of his sons?
answers: To ask him to prepare new incense
To tell him to leave his position
To explain the meaning of the event and emphasize the Lord’s glory
questions.explanation: Moses interprets their deaths as part of the Lord’s being sanctified before the people and emphasizes that holy service must honor Him.

paragraphs.title: Removing Aaron’s Sons from the Sanctuary

easy.question: Who called Mishael and Elzaphan?
answers: Moses
Aaron
Eleazar
easy.explanation: The passage says that Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan.

easy.question: Where did Mishael and Elzaphan carry their brothers?
answers: Into the tent of meeting
Outside the camp
To Aaron’s house
easy.explanation: Moses commanded them to carry their brothers outside the camp, and they did so.

easy.question: Who was commanded to mourn the burning?
answers: Mishael and Elzaphan
Aaron and his sons
The whole house of Israel
easy.explanation: Moses said that the people, the whole house of Israel, should mourn the burning.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Moses told Mishael and Elzaphan to carry out their brothers, and then gave instructions to Aaron and his sons
Aaron and his sons left the tent, and then Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan
All Israel carried out the brothers, and then Mishael and Elzaphan mourned
medium.explanation: First Moses commanded Mishael and Elzaphan to remove the dead men, and then he gave instructions to Aaron and his sons.

medium.question: In the phrase “Do not uncover your heads,” what did Moses forbid?
answers: Washing their heads
Interrupting the priests’ service
Uncovering or disarranging their hair as a sign of mourning
medium.explanation: In this mourning context, the command means that they were not to disarrange or uncover their hair as mourners normally did.

medium.question: Why were Aaron and his sons told not to leave the entrance of the tent of meeting?
answers: To search for Mishael and Elzaphan
So that all the people could enter the tent
Because the Lord’s anointing oil was upon them, and leaving could result in death
medium.explanation: The passage connects the command with the anointing oil upon them and warns, “lest ye die.”

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron”?
answers: Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron’s relatives
Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron’s sons
Mishael and Elzaphan were strangers to the camp
challenge.explanation: Uzziel was Aaron’s uncle, so his sons Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron’s cousins.

challenge.question: What was the contrast between Moses’ instructions to Aaron and his sons and his instructions to the whole house of Israel?
answers: Aaron and his sons had to leave the camp, while all Israel had to remain
Aaron and his sons were not to follow the usual mourning practices, while all Israel was to mourn
Aaron and his sons had to mourn, while all Israel had to remain silent
challenge.explanation: The priests were told not to uncover their heads or tear their clothes, while all Israel was told to mourn the burning.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the priests had to continue their duties despite the tragedy?
answers: They carried the dead men outside the camp
They left the tent of meeting to mourn
They were forbidden to leave the tent of meeting, and they obeyed Moses
challenge.explanation: The command to remain in the tent of meeting, and their obedience to it, show that the priests continued their sacred duty.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron”?
answers: Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron’s relatives
Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron’s sons
Mishael and Elzaphan were strangers to the camp
questions.explanation: Uzziel was Aaron’s uncle, so his sons Mishael and Elzaphan were Aaron’s cousins.

questions.question: What was the contrast between Moses’ instructions to Aaron and his sons and his instructions to the whole house of Israel?
answers: Aaron and his sons had to leave the camp, while all Israel had to remain
Aaron and his sons were not to follow the usual mourning practices, while all Israel was to mourn
Aaron and his sons had to mourn, while all Israel had to remain silent
questions.explanation: The priests were told not to uncover their heads or tear their clothes, while all Israel was told to mourn the burning.

questions.question: Which detail shows that the priests had to continue their duties despite the tragedy?
answers: They carried the dead men outside the camp
They left the tent of meeting to mourn
They were forbidden to leave the tent of meeting, and they obeyed Moses
questions.explanation: The command to remain in the tent of meeting, and their obedience to it, show that the priests continued their sacred duty.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition of Wine and Distinguishing the Holy

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak at the beginning of this passage?
answers: Aaron
Moses
The Israelites
easy.explanation: The passage begins by saying that the Lord spoke to Aaron.

easy.question: What were Aaron and his sons forbidden to drink?
answers: Water and juice
Wine and strong drink
Milk and honey
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded them not to drink wine or strong drink.

easy.question: What were the priests required to distinguish?
answers: Day from night
Israel from the nations
The holy from the common and the unclean from the clean
easy.explanation: The priests were commanded to distinguish between the holy and the common, and between the unclean and the clean.

medium.question: What reason is explicitly given for the prohibition against drinking before entering the tent of meeting?
answers: So that they would not die
So that they would not be hungry
So that they could rest
medium.explanation: The passage says that they must not drink when entering the tent of meeting, “lest ye die.”

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: Teach, drink, and then distinguish
Avoid wine, distinguish, and then teach
Distinguish, drink, and then teach
medium.explanation: First they are forbidden to drink wine and strong drink; then they are told to distinguish; finally they are to teach Israel.

medium.question: In the phrase “wine and strong drink,” what does “strong drink” mean?
answers: A sweet food
A special garment
An intoxicating beverage
medium.explanation: The term appears alongside wine in a prohibition against drinking, so it refers to an intoxicating beverage.

challenge.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the connection between the prohibition against drinking and the commands to distinguish and teach?
answers: The priests had to remain clear-minded so they could distinguish and teach properly
The priests did not need to learn the laws
Drinking helped the priests distinguish things
challenge.explanation: The verses connect the prohibition with the priests’ duties of distinguishing and teaching, suggesting that clear judgment was required.

challenge.question: What does the statement “a statute for ever throughout your generations” teach?
answers: The command lasted only a short time
The command was intended for future generations
The command applied only to Moses
challenge.explanation: The words “for ever” and “throughout your generations” emphasize that the law was to continue for future generations.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the phrase “which the Lord hath spoken unto them by the hand of Moses”?
answers: Moses received the laws from Aaron
The Israelites invented the laws themselves
Moses served as the messenger who conveyed the Lord’s words to Israel
challenge.explanation: The phrase “by the hand of Moses” indicates that the Lord communicated His words to Israel through Moses.

questions.question: What conclusion can be drawn from the connection between the prohibition against drinking and the commands to distinguish and teach?
answers: The priests had to remain clear-minded so they could distinguish and teach properly
The priests did not need to learn the laws
Drinking helped the priests distinguish things
questions.explanation: The verses connect the prohibition with the priests’ duties of distinguishing and teaching, suggesting that clear judgment was required.

questions.question: What does the statement “a statute for ever throughout your generations” teach?
answers: The command lasted only a short time
The command was intended for future generations
The command applied only to Moses
questions.explanation: The words “for ever” and “throughout your generations” emphasize that the law was to continue for future generations.

questions.question: What can be understood from the phrase “which the Lord hath spoken unto them by the hand of Moses”?
answers: Moses received the laws from Aaron
The Israelites invented the laws themselves
Moses served as the messenger who conveyed the Lord’s words to Israel
questions.explanation: The phrase “by the hand of Moses” indicates that the Lord communicated His words to Israel through Moses.

paragraphs.title: Eating the Offerings and Sacred Portions

easy.question: To whom did Moses speak at the beginning of this passage?
answers: Aaron, Eleazar, and Ithamar
Moses, Aaron, and Phinehas
All the Israelites
easy.explanation: Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s remaining sons.

easy.question: How was the remaining grain offering to be eaten?
answers: With leaven
Unleavened
Raw
easy.explanation: Moses commanded them to eat it unleavened.

easy.question: Who was allowed to eat the wave breast and the heave shoulder?
answers: All the Israelites
Moses alone
Aaron, his sons, and his daughters
easy.explanation: The passage says that these portions belonged to Aaron, his sons, and his daughters.

medium.question: In the phrase “it is thy due, and thy sons’ due,” what does “due” mean?
answers: The portion or right assigned to you
The house where you live
The punishment imposed on you
medium.explanation: Here, “due” means the portion assigned to Aaron and his sons as part of the offerings.

medium.question: Why was the grain offering to be eaten in a holy place?
answers: Because it was intended for all the people
Because it was most holy
Because it could not be brought to the altar
medium.explanation: The offering is called “most holy,” so it had to be eaten in a holy place.

medium.question: What sequence is described concerning the wave breast and the heave shoulder?
answers: They were eaten and only afterward brought as offerings
They were hidden from the priests
They were brought with the fat, waved before the Lord, and then assigned to Aaron and his sons
medium.explanation: The portions were brought with the fat, waved before the Lord, and then became a permanent portion for Aaron and his sons.

challenge.question: What was the main difference between where the grain offering and the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten?
answers: The grain offering was eaten in a holy place, while the breast and shoulder were eaten in a clean place
The grain offering was eaten anywhere, while the breast and shoulder were eaten only beside the altar
There was no difference
challenge.explanation: The grain offering was most holy and had to be eaten in a holy place, while the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten in a clean place.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the daughters are mentioned in verse 14, while Aaron and his sons are mentioned in verse 15?
answers: Only the daughters received a portion of the offerings
The verses identify the recipients according to the portion and its rules for eating
The sons were not allowed to eat at all
challenge.explanation: The verses do not list every family member in exactly the same way; verse 14 extends permission to eat the breast and shoulder to the daughters, while verse 15 emphasizes the permanent portion for Aaron and his sons.

challenge.question: Why does Moses emphasize that the portions were given to Aaron and his sons “by a statute for ever”?
answers: To say that the gift was only temporary
To cancel the command to wave them
To emphasize that this was a permanent right established by the Lord’s command
challenge.explanation: The phrase “by a statute for ever” shows that these portions were a lasting right for future generations, as the Lord commanded.

questions.question: What was the main difference between where the grain offering and the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten?
answers: The grain offering was eaten in a holy place, while the breast and shoulder were eaten in a clean place
The grain offering was eaten anywhere, while the breast and shoulder were eaten only beside the altar
There was no difference
questions.explanation: The grain offering was most holy and had to be eaten in a holy place, while the wave breast and heave shoulder were eaten in a clean place.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the fact that the daughters are mentioned in verse 14, while Aaron and his sons are mentioned in verse 15?
answers: Only the daughters received a portion of the offerings
The verses identify the recipients according to the portion and its rules for eating
The sons were not allowed to eat at all
questions.explanation: The verses do not list every family member in exactly the same way; verse 14 extends permission to eat the breast and shoulder to the daughters, while verse 15 emphasizes the permanent portion for Aaron and his sons.

questions.question: Why does Moses emphasize that the portions were given to Aaron and his sons “by a statute for ever”?
answers: To say that the gift was only temporary
To cancel the command to wave them
To emphasize that this was a permanent right established by the Lord’s command
questions.explanation: The phrase “by a statute for ever” shows that these portions were a lasting right for future generations, as the Lord commanded.

paragraphs.title: Searching for the Sin Offering and the Rebuke

easy.question: Whom was Moses angry with?
answers: Eleazar and Ithamar
Aaron and all his sons
The elders of the people
easy.explanation: Moses was angry with Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron’s surviving sons.

easy.question: What had Eleazar and Ithamar not eaten?
answers: The daily offering
The goat of the sin offering
The fine-flour offering
easy.explanation: Moses asked why they had not eaten the sin offering in the holy place.

easy.question: Where was the sin offering supposed to be eaten?
answers: Outside the camp
In Aaron’s house
In the holy place
easy.explanation: The passage says that it was to be eaten in the holy place.

medium.question: Why, according to Moses, were the priests supposed to eat the sin offering?
answers: To celebrate the completion of the service
To bear the iniquity of the congregation and make atonement for it
So that no meat would remain in the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The sin offering was given to the priests so that they could bear the congregation’s iniquity and make atonement for it before the Lord.

medium.question: In the phrase “to bear the iniquity of the congregation,” what does “bear” mean?
answers: To lift the offering with their hands
To remove the people from the sanctuary
To accept responsibility for making atonement for the congregation
medium.explanation: The following words, “to make atonement for them,” show that “bear” means to accept responsibility for atonement, not merely to lift something.

medium.question: Which detail explained why the priests were permitted to eat the sin offering in the holy place?
answers: Its blood had not been brought inside the sanctuary
It was not an important offering
It had been prepared outside the camp
medium.explanation: Moses emphasized that its blood had not been brought inside the sanctuary; therefore, the priests were to eat it in the holy place.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary” and “ye should indeed have eaten it in the holy place”?
answers: Every offering eaten in the holy place had to be burned
The priests were not allowed to touch the offering
The treatment of the offering was determined by how its blood was used
challenge.explanation: When the blood of the sin offering was not brought inside, its meat was to be eaten in the holy place; the verse connects the location of the blood with the rule for the meat.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “most holy” indicate about the sin offering?
answers: It was an offering of special holiness requiring proper treatment
It was intended only for the whole people to eat
It had nothing to do with atonement
challenge.explanation: The phrase “most holy” emphasizes the offering’s special holiness and the requirement that it be eaten in the proper place and manner.

challenge.question: Why did Moses address Eleazar and Ithamar rather than the whole people?
answers: Because they were the priests responsible for eating the offering
Because they were the only people left in the camp
Because they had prepared the blood of the sin offering
challenge.explanation: Eleazar and Ithamar were Aaron’s surviving sons and priests, so they bore responsibility for eating the offering and making atonement.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between “its blood was not brought inside the sanctuary” and “ye should indeed have eaten it in the holy place”?
answers: Every offering eaten in the holy place had to be burned
The priests were not allowed to touch the offering
The treatment of the offering was determined by how its blood was used
questions.explanation: When the blood of the sin offering was not brought inside, its meat was to be eaten in the holy place; the verse connects the location of the blood with the rule for the meat.

questions.question: What does the phrase “most holy” indicate about the sin offering?
answers: It was an offering of special holiness requiring proper treatment
It was intended only for the whole people to eat
It had nothing to do with atonement
questions.explanation: The phrase “most holy” emphasizes the offering’s special holiness and the requirement that it be eaten in the proper place and manner.

questions.question: Why did Moses address Eleazar and Ithamar rather than the whole people?
answers: Because they were the priests responsible for eating the offering
Because they were the only people left in the camp
Because they had prepared the blood of the sin offering
questions.explanation: Eleazar and Ithamar were Aaron’s surviving sons and priests, so they bore responsibility for eating the offering and making atonement.

easy.question: Who spoke to Moses in verse 19?
answers: Aaron
Nadab
Eleazar
easy.explanation: The verse begins by saying, “And Aaron said unto Moses.”

easy.question: What offerings had been made that day?
answers: Peace offerings and a grain offering
A sin offering and a burnt offering
A Passover offering and a thank offering
easy.explanation: Aaron said, “This day have they offered their sin offering and their burnt offering before the Lord.”

easy.question: How did Moses respond to Aaron’s words?
answers: He became angry
He remained silent
He was satisfied with the explanation
easy.explanation: The passage ends by saying that Moses heard this and was content.

medium.question: Why did Aaron ask whether it would have been accepted by the Lord if he had eaten the sin offering?
answers: He wanted to know whether eating it had been appropriate
He did not know what had been offered
Moses had asked him to eat it
medium.explanation: Aaron explained his actions and asked whether eating the sin offering on that day would have been acceptable before the Lord.

medium.question: In the phrase “should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord?”, what does “accepted” mean?
answers: Considered good or pleasing
Made faster
Kept hidden
medium.explanation: The question asks whether the act would have been considered good and acceptable in the Lord’s sight.

medium.question: What happened according to the order of events in Aaron’s statement?
answers: Moses listened, and then Aaron made the offerings
The offerings were made, events happened to Aaron, and he considered eating the sin offering
Aaron ate first, and then the offerings were made
medium.explanation: Aaron first describes the offerings made that day, then what had happened to him, and finally the question of eating the sin offering.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Moses hearing Aaron’s explanation and being satisfied with it?
answers: Aaron’s explanation was accepted
Moses did not understand him
Aaron was punished for eating the offering
challenge.explanation: Moses’ positive response shows that he accepted Aaron’s explanation.

challenge.question: Which detail in Aaron’s words emphasizes that the event took place on a special day?
answers: The words “this day”
The name “Moses”
The words “in his sight”
challenge.explanation: Aaron repeats the reference to “this day,” highlighting the special occasion on which the offerings were made and the events occurred.

challenge.question: What does Aaron’s question, “should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord?”, reveal about his thinking?
answers: He cared only about his personal wishes
He wanted to evaluate his action according to the Lord’s will
He wanted to replace Moses
challenge.explanation: Aaron did not rely only on his own judgment; he asked whether the action was acceptable in the Lord’s sight.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Moses hearing Aaron’s explanation and being satisfied with it?
answers: Aaron’s explanation was accepted
Moses did not understand him
Aaron was punished for eating the offering
questions.explanation: Moses’ positive response shows that he accepted Aaron’s explanation.

questions.question: Which detail in Aaron’s words emphasizes that the event took place on a special day?
answers: The words “this day”
The name “Moses”
The words “in his sight”
questions.explanation: Aaron repeats the reference to “this day,” highlighting the special occasion on which the offerings were made and the events occurred.

questions.question: What does Aaron’s question, “should it have been accepted in the sight of the Lord?”, reveal about his thinking?
answers: He cared only about his personal wishes
He wanted to evaluate his action according to the Lord’s will
He wanted to replace Moses
questions.explanation: Aaron did not rely only on his own judgment; he asked whether the action was acceptable in the Lord’s sight.
